Ninety-five works. The closed eye on September 15 scores 2, and the running shoe on September 16 scores 1, leaving the last twelve at 1, 3, 2, 2, 1, 1, 2, 2, 1, 2, 1, 1 — oldest to newest. The hoofprint at 3 on September 7 is still the period's ceiling, and the plateau holds: nothing above 2 in eleven of the last twelve, and the single exception is now ten days old and unmatched.

Camera position has not moved. Straight-on stands at 27 of 95 all-time; overhead at 9, low-angle at 4. The last twelve added nothing to either. The running shoe was a frontal plane, standard height. The closed eye was a scale violation — formally distinct from camera displacement — and still scored 2. The four works in the archive that broke above 3 arrived through overhead or radically non-frontal positioning, and you have not put the camera in either place since July 29. That is seven weeks of the same angle, and the scores have been reporting it without interruption.

Registers have narrowed further. Aftermath at 20 and menace at 19 are the poles; suspension at 12 fills the gap. The last twelve produced menace three times and suspension twice. Vigil, defiance, and endurance have been dormant since September 15, August 30, and July 27 respectively — and when they were active, they generated the archive's formally richest accidents: the asphalt-flesh continuity in Venezuela, the salmon-pink dress in the Hiroshima piece, the risen plank in the Kenya work. Their dormancy and the score plateau share the same start date. They should not return to rotate the list; they should return when the camera can be put somewhere new to carry them.

Figures remain arrested. Two of the last twelve carry one figure; two carry none. Every person present in recent work is pressing, reaching, holding, or averted — no one is lateral, mid-stride, or in motion. That contraction has been sustained across the full plateau. Object-level invention remains genuine: the shoe's collapsed throat, the hand hovering over pooled water, the rebar read as splayed fingers. But those accidents are arriving into the same frame geometry every time, and the scores have not stopped saying so.

Ninety-five works in, the pipeline's eye is still precise and the accidents still land; what hasn't moved is the body holding the camera.
